steps.title: The Character studio
steps.body: The Characters workspace dresses minifigures (hair, face, outfit, colors, gear) and animates them with keyframe clips. The hero and every neighbour are characters.

steps.title: A new character
steps.body: Every hero starts from one of v68’s presets: + New character shows a picture of each one; click the one you want. The copy is yours to change; presets themselves stay as they are. An explorer suits a treasure hunt.
steps.task: Click + New character, then click the picture “Explorer”.

steps.title: Change the look
steps.body: This chapter, Logic and Cinematics make one scene together: your hero walks up to a treasure chest, opens it, a sword rises out of it with a fanfare, and the hero holds it up. First the hero. Each choice in the panel on the right (hair, hat, shirt…) is a button with a picture; it opens pictures of your character wearing each option.
steps.task: Name your hero Rowan, then give Rowan a cowboy hat.

how.text: In the panel “Character” (right), click the box “Name”, select its text, type Rowan and press Enter. The title above the preview and the name in the list on the left change to Rowan.

do.say: Type Rowan in the box “Name” (right) and press Enter.

how.text: Scroll the same panel to the section “Face & hair” and click the button “Hat” (it shows a small picture of the hat your character wears now). A panel of pictures opens: your character wearing each hat.

do.say: Click the button “Hat” under “Face & hair”: a panel of hat pictures opens.

how.text: In that panel, click the picture “Cowboy hat”. The panel closes, the preview wears the cowboy hat, and the button “Hat” now reads “Cowboy hat”.

do.say: Click the picture “Cowboy hat”: the preview wears it.

steps.title: The player character
steps.body: One character is the hero the player controls, and every cinematic’s “hero” role is played by it. “Make player character” (or Project tab › Hero) picks it.

how.text: In the panel “Character” (right), under the name, click the button “Make player character”. It turns into “Player character” and the list on the left marks Rowan as the player.

do.say: Click “Make player character” under the name: Rowan is the hero now.

steps.title: A clip: Open chest
steps.body: A clip is a short movement made of keys: at a moment, a joint has a value (how far an arm is turned). Rowan needs two: “Open chest” (reach down, lift the lid) and “Hold it up” (both arms up with the sword). Clips that play once and then hold their last pose have Loop off.
steps.task: Make a clip named “Open chest”, 1.6 s long, that does not loop.

how.text: In the list on the left, next to “Clips”, click “+ New”. A clip named “New clip” opens under “Mine”, with an empty timeline under the preview.

do.say: Click “+ New” next to “Clips” (left): a new clip opens.

how.text: In the panel on the right, section “Clip”, click the box “Clip name”, type Open chest and press Enter. The list on the left shows “Open chest” under “Mine”.

do.say: Type Open chest in “Clip name” (right) and press Enter.

how.text: In the timeline tools (the bar under the preview), untick “Loop”: the clip plays once and holds its last pose, as a cinematic needs.

do.say: Untick “Loop” in the timeline tools: the clip plays once.

how.text: In the timeline tools, click the box “Length”, type 1.6 and press Enter. The time at the left reads “… / 1.60 s”.

do.say: Type 1.6 in “Length” and press Enter: the clip lasts 1.6 s.

steps.title: Animate: reach and lift
steps.body: A track moves one joint; its keys say where the joint is at each moment, and the clip eases between them. “Right arm · x” swings the arm forward (negative) or back. Click a track’s name and the preview rings that part. “⇆ Mirror” copies a track to the other side, so both arms move together.
steps.task: Right arm · x: −1.3 at 0.5 s (reach), −2.4 at 1.1 s (lift); mirror it to the left arm; press Play.

how.text: In the timeline tools, open the drop-down “+ Track…” and pick “Right arm · x”. A lane appears with a key ◆ at 0 s; it is selected, so the preview rings the right arm.

do.say: Open “+ Track…” and pick “Right arm · x”: the right arm is ringed.

how.text: Click the lanes a quarter of the way across, so the time at the left reads about 0.50 / 1.60 s.

do.say: Click the lanes at 0.50 s: the playhead moves there.

how.text: Click “◆ Key”. A key appears at 0.5 s and is selected: its “at” and “value” boxes show under the lanes.

do.click: [aria-label="Timeline tools"] button[title="Key the selected track at the playhead"]
do.say: Click “◆ Key”: a key at 0.5 s, selected.

how.text: Under the lanes, click the box “value”, select its text, type -1.3 and press Enter. The arm reaches forward and down, and the lane shows −1.3 next to the key.

do.say: Type -1.3 in “value” and press Enter: the arm reaches forward.

how.text: Click the lanes about two thirds of the way across, so the time reads about 1.10 / 1.60 s.

do.say: Click the lanes at 1.10 s.

how.text: Click “◆ Key” again: a second key at 1.1 s, selected.

do.click: [aria-label="Timeline tools"] button[title="Key the selected track at the playhead"]
do.say: Click “◆ Key”: a key at 1.1 s.

how.text: In “value”, type -2.4 and press Enter: the arm lifts up in front (the lid goes up with it).

do.say: Type -2.4 in “value” and press Enter: the arm lifts.

how.text: Click “⇆ Mirror” in the timeline tools. A lane “Left arm · x” appears with the same keys: both arms reach and lift together.

do.say: Click “⇆ Mirror”: the left arm gets the same keys.

how.text: Press “Play” at the top right of the preview: Rowan reaches down and lifts, then holds.

do.say: Press “Play” (top right of the preview) to watch it.

steps.title: A clip: Hold it up
steps.body: The second clip raises both arms above the head, the way a hero shows off what they found. “Right arm · z” turns the arm out to the side and up; “⇆ Mirror” turns the left one the other way, so both go up.
steps.task: Make a clip “Hold it up”, 4 s, Loop off: Right arm · z at 2.9 from 0.5 s, mirrored, then Play.

how.text: Next to “Clips” (left), click “+ New”. A new clip opens.

do.say: Click “+ New” next to “Clips”.

how.text: In “Clip name” (right, section “Clip”), type Hold it up and press Enter.

do.say: Type Hold it up in “Clip name” and press Enter.

how.text: In the timeline tools, untick “Loop”.

do.say: Untick “Loop”.

how.text: In the timeline tools, in “Length”, type 4 and press Enter: the arms stay up for the rest of the scene (a clip that does not loop ends when its time is up).

do.say: Type 4 in “Length” and press Enter.

how.text: Open “+ Track…” and pick “Right arm · z”. The right arm is ringed in the preview.

do.say: Pick “Right arm · z” in “+ Track…”.

how.text: Click the lanes a quarter of the way across (about 0.50 s).

do.say: Click the lanes at 0.50 s.

how.text: Click “◆ Key”: a key at 0.5 s, selected.

do.click: [aria-label="Timeline tools"] button[title="Key the selected track at the playhead"]
do.say: Click “◆ Key”.

how.text: In “value” (under the lanes), type 2.9 and press Enter: the right arm points up, and stays up to the end (after the last key a track holds its value).

do.say: Type 2.9 in “value” and press Enter: the arm goes up.

how.text: Click “⇆ Mirror”: “Left arm · z” gets −2.9, so the left arm goes up too.

do.say: Click “⇆ Mirror”: both arms go up.

how.text: Press “Play” (top right of the preview): both arms rise and stay up.

do.say: Press “Play” to watch it.
